name: Armenian Center for Contemporary Experimental Art (ACCEA/NPAK)
funding: Small diaspora-funded NGO (US 501(c)(3) since 1995) with benefactors incl. Balassanian, Cafesjian, Boghossian, Hovnanian funds; state gives building free since 2002.

name: Cafesjian Center for the Arts
funding: Gerard Cafesjian, a former West Publishing executive, renovated the Cascade site and opened the centre in 2009.

name: Modern Art Museum of Yerevan
funding: Small museum founded in 1972 with the city's backing and listed among Yerevan municipality's museums; its current funder roster is not published.

name: National Gallery of Armenia
funding: A state gallery on Republic Square, founded in 1921 and run under Armenia's Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sports; its budget and sponsors were not found.

name: Samstag Museum of Art
funding: Adelaide University museum, founded in 2007 by the University of South Australia. The Samstag bequest funds scholarships it administers. Partners: Adelaide Festival, Adelaide Film Festival, The Lane Vineyard.

name: Murray Art Museum Albury
funding: AlburyCity Council and Create NSW. Major benefactors: Paul Ramsay Foundation, Russell Mills Foundation, Metal Manufacturers and the Colin and Lorraine Joss family. MAMA Art Foundation raises acquisition funds.

name: Art Gallery of Ballarat
funding: City of Ballarat with Creative Victoria. Also named: Ian Potter, Sidney Myer, Buckland, Helen Macpherson Smith, Gandel, McCain, Mars and NAB.

name: Bendigo Art Gallery
funding: $45M redevelopment (2025): $21M Victoria, $9M City of Greater Bendigo, Sidney Myer Fund $4M, Ian Potter $3M; partners La Trobe University, Innes, Balgownie, Mercure.

name: Institute of Modern Art
funding: Arts Queensland and Creative Australia. Partners include Sullivan+Strumpf, The Calile Hotel, Coopers, Bird in Hand, Autex and Creative Brisbane Collab.

name: QAGOMA
funding: Queensland Government statutory body. Funders: Creative Australia, Shayher Group, Carnival Cruise Line, Tim Fairfax Family Foundation.
